OG-15.from: In a grid-down winter scenario, hypothermia is a real threat within hours — not days. A warm home is not just about comfort; it is about survival.
OG-15.to: In a winter power cut, a cold home can become a health risk — especially for babies, older people and anyone with a health condition. A warm, dry home is about health, not just comfort.
OG-15.reason: Owner ruling 5.1 and 5.2: no official source gives 'within hours' for a cold home (removed); 'about survival' replaced with the owner's wording. Groups at risk: Health NZ and Better Health Channel (Vic).

OG-15.from: 3. Bedrooms comfortable for sleeping (16–18°C) without excessive heating
OG-15.to: 3. Bedrooms stay comfortably warm overnight without excessive heating
OG-15.reason: Owner ruling 5.3: the 16–18°C adult-bedroom figure is unsupported (16°C appears only in guidance for a baby's room). No new figure added.

OG-15.where: Heating cost reality check — claims 4 and 5
OG-15.from: Every 1°C you lower your thermostat saves approximately 10% on heating bills. A home heated to 21°C costs roughly 30% more than one heated to 18°C.
OG-15.to: Each extra degree of heating uses more energy, so heat to a healthy temperature rather than a higher one.
OG-15.reason: Owner rulings 5.4 and 5.5: the '10%' overstates energy.gov.au (5–10%) and EECA gives no percentage, so the statement is non-numeric; the derived '30%' claim is removed.
